title: Servicing manual for CNC PCs with Windows 10 IoT Enterprise (Cnc886 control PC)

pages.text:
Windows 10 IoT Enterprise
servicing manual
Servicing manual for PCs with Windows 10 IoT 
Enterprise
Preamble
Windows 10 IoT Enterprise is specialized edition of Windows 10 aimed at deployment in industry. 
Most prominent feature is long-term security support without function updates. This provides stable
environment for CNC control system,
System storage (solid-state drive) is separated to two partitions C: and D:. Partition C:  is for system
and applications, partition D: is for user data. Partition C: can protected against changes with 
Universal Write Filter1 (UWF). As such, it is necessary to follow instructions in order to make 
changes that would otherwise be removed on reset by UWF.
Configuration Details
User accounts
System contains following predefined user accounts:
•
admin (Machine Administrator)
◦default password admin
◦system administrator account controlled by customer
•
operator (Machine Operator)
◦no password
◦limited user for machine operation
•
servicing (Service Support)
◦password set by manufactured, must not be changed
◦system administrator account for manufacturer
Software preinstalled by vendor
•
IntervalZero RTX – Windows real-time extension, required for Cnc886
•
7-Zip – archive manager
•
Notepad++ – advanced text editor
1
More information available at https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/customize/enterprise/unified-
write-filter

•
ImageGlass – simple image viewer
•
SumatraPDF – simple PDF viewer
•
TeamViewer – remote support tool
Source code for open source programs is included in the installation in C:\Install.
Additional software
Any additional software must be approved by machine vendor prior installation. No warranty for 
compatibility is provided without previous testing.
Support scripts
Folder C:\Program Files\Tools contains number of scripts for system maintenance.
•
commit_cnc886.ps1(cmd)– save changed files in C:\Cnc886 folder when UWF is enabled.
•
set_network_private.ps1 – Switches network profile to Private tin order to enable file 
sharing services.
•
updates_install(_restart).ps1 – Search and install all Windows updates (and automatically 
reboot computer).
•
updates_cleanup(_restart).ps1 – Remove unnecessary files left by Windows Update (and 
automatically reboot computer).
•
uwf-disable.ps1(cmd) – Disable Universal Write Filter.
•
uwf-enable.ps1(cmd) – Enable Universal Write Filter.
Further configuration details
•
Windows Updates are controlled by customer IT management.
•
Windows Defender files are relocated to hidden folder D:\WinDefend in order to keep these 
files writable even with UWF enabled.
•
Remote Desktop is enabled for administrator accounts.
•
During system start-up prompt appears enabling to choose between “Windows 10 – RTX” or
„Windows 10“. For regular operation “Windows 10 – RTX” must be selected. This option is 
default and will be automatically selected after 5 seconds.
Details regarding the control application Cnc886
•
Program files and most of the configuration files are stored in C:\Cnc886.
•
Additional configuration files are stored in D:\config.
•
CNC programs are stored in D:\cncfiles.
◦This folder is by default shared with read/write access for Everyone.
•
Other user data are stored on drive D:.

Basic computer operation
•
Power on: computer is configured to power on automatically as soon as machine is powered 
up.
•
Power off: Switch Cnc886 to Blocked state, terminate Cnc886, shut down main power 
switch (optionally you may first shut down Windows via Start>Power Icon>Shutdown)
•
Reboot: Switch Cnc886 to Blocked state, terminate Cnc886,  reboot Windows via 
Start>Power Icon>Restart
How to make changes – standard procedures with UWF 
enabled
Making changes requires administrative privileges. Either the system requests them automatically 
or you must run given command as an administrator. If you are logged in as Operator, you will be 
prompted with dialog offering to log in as admin or servicing user. If you are already logged in as 
administrative account, you will be prompted with confirmation dialog.
Making changes in Cnc886 folder
Following steps are necessary to preserve changed files in folder C:\Cnc886. Files on drive D: are 
always preserved.
1. Terminate Cnc886 application
2. Perform needed changes (replace files, modify .knf files, …)
3. Run script C:\Program Files\Tools\commit_cnc886.ps1 (right click > Run with 
PowerShell).
4. Script will request administrative privileges. 
5. Reboot the system once the script is finished.
6. Verify that changes are preserved.
Changing system configuration
Following steps are necessary to change Windows configuration (e. g. network settings, user profile
modifications, …)
1. Disable UWF.
•
Run script C:\Program Files\Tools\uwf_disable.ps1 (right click > Run with 
PowerShell).
•
System will reboot.
2. After reboot, the UWF filter is disabled and all changes from this point forward will be 
saved to disk.
3. Perform all required changes.
4. Reboot computer.

5. Enable UWF.
•
Run script C:\Program Files\Tools\uwf_enable.ps1 (right click > Run with 
PowerShell).
•
System will reboot.
6. After reboot, the UWF filter is enabled and any changes will be discarded on reboot.
Updating Windows
Note: Windows Update require Internet connection. Update process can take a long time during 
which the machine should not be used.
Before installing updates, check with machine vendor if updates have been tested for compatibility 
issues.
1. Disable UWF.
•
Run script C:\Program Files\Tools\uwf_disable.ps1 (right click > Run with 
PowerShell).
•
Press ENTER to reboot system.
2. After reboot, the UWF filter is disabled and all changes from this point forward will be 
saved to disk.
3. Run script C:\Program Files\Tools\updates_install(_restart).ps1 (right click > Run with 
PowerShell).
4. Once finished, reboot system and wait for updates to finish.
5. Repeat steps 3 and 4 as long as new updates show up. Repeat these steps at least twice.
6. Run script C:\Program Files\Tools\updates_cleanup(_restart).ps1 (right click > Run with 
PowerShell).
7. Once finished, reboot system..
8. Enable UWF.
•
Run script C:\Program Files\Tools\uwf_enable.ps1 (right click > Run with 
PowerShell).
•
Press ENTER to reboot system.
9. After reboot, the UWF filter is enabled and any changes will be discarded on reboot.
Configuring network address
Configuration of network requires disabled UWF, see chapter “Changing system configuration“.
1. Open Network and Sharing Center by right-click on network icon.

2. Open “Change adapter settings”
3. Open Properties of chosen adapter. Administrator login is required.
4. IP address can be changed under Internet Protocol Version 4 (TCP/IPv4)
5. Confirm all changes, reboot computer to verify it, and re-enable UWF.
Backup
•
Critical files are Cnc886 configuration files. We recommend periodical backup of whole C:\
Cnc886 folder.

•
Backup regime for CNC files (stored in D:\cncfiles) is up to customer requirements.
•
Additional data on D: drive (with the exception of D:\WinDefend folder) shall be backed up 
as necessary.
•
Complete system backup can be performed by any available disk cloning tool. Tested tools 
include CloneZilla, Windows DISM disk capture using Windows PE.
Recommendations
•
Restart computer periodically. Do not leave the system running for long periods. UWF 
consumes RAM and long periods of operation can consume all available RAM rendering the
system unstable or unusable.
Known issues
•
During boot, system keeps performing disk check on drive C:.
◦Skip disk check by pressing key when prompted.
◦Disable UWF and restart system.
◦Let the disk check run to completion.
◦Re-enable UWF and continue using the system.
